title: Metabolomics and molecular dynamics unveil the therapeutic potential of epalrestat in diabetic nephropathy.
authors: Song, Tongtong; Wang, Rongjin; Zhou, Xiaoyue; Chen, Weijia; Chen, Ying; Liu, Zhongying; Men, Lihui
one_liner_zh: 该文研究依帕司他对糖尿病肾病的治疗机制，涉及代谢组学与分子动力学，但对象为小分子-蛋白互作，非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，与本课题无关。
abstract: Diabetic nephropathy (DN) is one of the leading clinical causes of end-stage renal failure. The classical aldose reductase (AR) inhibitor epalrestat shows beneficial effect on renal dysfunction induced by DN, with metabolic profile and molecular mechanisms remains to be investigated further. In the current study, integrated untargeted metabolomics, network pharmacology and molecular dynamics approaches were applied to explore the therapeutic mechanisms of epalrestat against DN. Firstly, untargeted serum and urine metabolomics analysis based on UPLC-Q-TOF-MS was performed, revealed that epalrestat could regulate the metabolic disorders of amino acids metabolism, arachidonic acid metabolism, pyrimidine metabolism and citrate cycle metabolism pathways after DN. Subsequently, metabolomics-based network analysis was carried out to predict potential active targets of epalrestat, mainly involving AGE-RAGE signaling pathway, TNF signaling pathway and HIF-1 signaling pathway. Moreover, a 100 ns molecular dynamics approach was employed to validate the interactions between epalrestat and the core targets, showing that epalrestat could form remarkable tight binding with GLUT1 and NFkappaB than it with AR. Surface-plasmon resonance assay further verified epalrestat could bind GLUT1 and NFkappaB proteins specifically. Overall, integrated system network analysis not only demonstrated that epalrestat could attenuate DN induced metabolic disorders and renal injuries, but also revealed that it could interact with multi-targets to play a synergistic regulatory role in the treatment of DN.
abstract_zh: 糖尿病肾病（DN）是导致终末期肾衰竭的主要临床原因之一。经典的醛糖还原酶（AR）抑制剂依帕司他对DN引起的肾功能障碍显示出有益效果，但其代谢特征和分子机制仍需进一步研究。在本研究中，采用整合的非靶向代谢组学、网络药理学和分子动力学方法，探讨依帕司他抗DN的治疗机制。首先，基于UPLC-Q-TOF-MS的血清和尿液非靶向代谢组学分析显示，依帕司他能够调节DN后氨基酸代谢、花生四烯酸代谢、嘧啶代谢和柠檬酸循环代谢通路的代谢紊乱。随后，进行基于代谢组学的网络分析，以预测依帕司他的潜在活性靶点，主要涉及AGE-RAGE信号通路、TNF信号通路和HIF-1信号通路。此外，采用100 ns的分子动力学方法验证依帕司他与核心靶点之间的相互作用，结果表明依帕司他与GLUT1和NFkappaB的结合比其与AR的结合更为紧密。表面等离子体共振实验进一步证实依帕司他能够特异性结合GLUT1和NFkappaB蛋白。总体而言，整合的系统网络分析不仅证明了依帕司他能够减轻DN诱导的代谢紊乱和肾损伤，还揭示了其可通过与多靶点相互作用在DN治疗中发挥协同调节作用。
